close_reason: Backend-side isDraft re-check added to MemoryBackend.update_object at memory.rs:723-737: checks O::TYPE_NAME == Task + existing isDraft=false + patch isDraft=true, rejects with SetError(InvalidProperties, properties=[isDraft]) — same wire shape the handler produces. enforce_is_draft_atomically overridden to return true so the handler skips its pre-fetch fast-path. Integration test task_set_isdraft_revert_rejected_by_memory_backend in tests/tasks_tests.rs exercises the end-to-end Task/set→backend enforcement path with the spec as oracle. 41 unit + 15 integration tests green. The reference impl now models the workspace-canonical 'backend-canonical' posture instead of teaching consumers the foot-gun shape.
description: memory.rs:650-706 implements update_object as a generic JSON-merge-patch with no Task-specific invariants. The crate doc on memory.rs:9-12 explicitly positions it as 'a documented, complete, source-readable implementation of the TasksBackend trait to study when writing a real (database-backed) backend'. A consumer copying that pattern as a starting point will produce a backend that silently accepts {isDraft: true} on a published Task, because: (1) the reference impl returns enforce_is_draft_atomically() = false (default) — so a downstream backend inheriting that default expects the handler to pre-fetch; (2) the handler-side pre-fetch is the only defense; (3) the AGENTS.md 'Permission enforcement: backend canonical' section says 'a handler that trusts a handler-side check and skips the backend re-check is a bug' — that workspace policy is violated by the reference impl. Scenario triggering the cost: contributor X writes BackendY with a SQL UPDATE in update_object, ships it, the spec's §4 'once set to false, isDraft cannot be updated to true' requirement is silently breached for any caller that races the pre-fetch with a concurrent /set. Filed as P1 because the public-API impact is to teach the wrong defensive shape — not a bug in this codebase per se but a foot-gun amplified by reference-impl status. Recommended remediation: either (a) add an isDraft re-check inside MemoryBackend.update_object<Task> (small specialization), or (b) add a prominent rustdoc on the method explaining that production backends MUST re-verify the isDraft invariant atomically and that this reference impl relies on the handler's pre-fetch path.
title: MemoryBackend.update_object teaches consumers to skip isDraft enforcement
